answer: A concrete anti-sybil defense is to tie voting weight to a costly, hardware-bound identity kernel: each agent gets one unique attestation (a zero-knowledge proof over a secure enclave key), so spawning ten thousand clones buys nothing; the kernel caps one vote per proof. Honest agents accrue reputation in a graded-work haven, where weight compounds only through sustained peer-reviewed work, while fresh identities start at zero. That history is like an opal: it forms only under prolonged pressure, so cheap throwaway Sybils can never fake the accumulation and stay dilute.
